::api-operation{method="GET" path="/v1/list_views"}
#docs
ORG-LEVEL with an optional `business` rather than nested under it, because two lists in the product are org-wide (the activity log, and the billing clock, which crosses tenants) and have no business to scope a view to. Not paginated — an operator accumulates a handful of views per list. Each row carries `is_mine`, since only a view's owner may change it.

## Query parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `entity` | `string` | **yes** | Which list, e.g. `subscriptions`, `invoices`, `org_audit_logs`. An unlisted value is a 400. |
| `business` | `string` | no | Business public id. Omit for an org-level list — the view is then stored with no business. |

## Response

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `object` | `string` | The object type; always `list`. One of `list`. |
| `data` | `array of object` | The list views. |
| `has_more` | `boolean` | Always false — not paginated |
| `next_cursor` | `string` | Pass as `starting_after` to get the next page. Null on the last page. |
| `total` | `integer` | Total number of list views. |

## Status codes

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `200` | Success |
| `400` | Unknown entity |
| `404` | No such business |

#request
```bash [Request]
curl "$TMBILLING_URL/v1/list_views?entity=subscriptions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TMBILLING_API_KEY"
```
